accepted.question: Explain the Samy worm as a case study of a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack, including its propagation technique and impact.

marking_points.point: The Samy worm injects JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It obtains the list of a user's heroes via a GET request on a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user's heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It adds Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile gets their profile infected with JavaScript and their friends list infected with Samy.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user's page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The worm eventually infected about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The attack exploits the fact that any web application returning user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

accepted.question: Explain the two rules of the Chinese Wall model.

marking_points.point: The simple security rule permits access only if the object is in the same company dataset as previously accessed objects or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: A subject s can be granted access to an object o only if the object: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s, that is, "within the Wall," or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: The *-property permits write access only if the simple security rule is satisfied and no object can be read that is in a different company dataset and contains unsanitized information.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

marking_points.point: ACLs and capabilities are the most common practical access control instruments.

marking_points.point: ACLs are used in Windows security, where a DACL is a list of Access Control Entries (ACEs).

questions.question: Explain the Samy worm as a case study of a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack, including its propagation technique and impact.

marking_points.point: The Samy worm injects JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It obtains the list of a user's heroes via a GET request on a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It adds Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile gets their profile infected with JavaScript and their friends list infected with Samy.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The worm eventually infected about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The attack exploits the fact that any web application returning user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Based on the scenario in (a), discuss how the ACM Code of Ethics and professional conduct guides an organization in protecting employee privacy and fulfilling its responsibility to safeguard personal data.

marking_points.point: The ACM Code of Ethics provides a documented set of acceptable behaviors that defines appropriate and inappropriate actions for the organization regarding privacy.
marking_points.quote: Documented set of acceptable behaviors for professional or social groups.

marking_points.point: The organization must follow the guiding beliefs and standards of ethics to ensure privacy protection is part of its professional conduct.
marking_points.quote: Ethics is a suite of guiding beliefs, standards, or ideals that pervades an individual or a group or community of people

marking_points.point: The organization must comply with formal rules of conduct, such as privacy laws, imposed by government authorities.
marking_points.quote: Laws are formal rules of conduct that a sovereign authority, such as a government, imposes on its subjects or citizens

marking_points.point: The ACM Code of Ethics, as an example of a code of ethics, provides a framework for professional conduct that includes privacy responsibilities.
marking_points.quote: Association of Computing Machinery ACM (founded 1947) has a code of ethics and professional conduct.

marking_points.point: The organization must identify specific actions as appropriate or inappropriate to ensure privacy is respected in its handling of employee data.
marking_points.quote: Identifies specific actions as appropriate or inappropriate.

marking_points.point: The organization's responsibility to protect privacy is rooted in the moral tradition of doing what is right, which underpins ethical behavior.
marking_points.quote: Morals are traditions of belief about right and wrong conduct and “doing what is morally right” is the bedrock of our social behavior

questions.question: Compare access control matrix (ACM), access control lists (ACL), and capabilities as access control structures, identifying their key characteristics and practical use.

marking_points.point: ACM, ACL, and capabilities are all access control structures for implementing access policies.
marking_points.quote: Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies: access control matrix (ACM) Capabilities (C-List) access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.point: ACLs and capabilities are the most common practical access control instruments.
marking_points.quote: Most common practical access control instruments are ACLs, capabilities and various abstractions.

marking_points.point: ACLs are used in Windows security, where a DACL is a list of Access Control Entries (ACEs).
marking_points.quote: DACL in a security descriptor is a list of Access Control Entries (ACE)

marking_points.point: ACLs can be inherited from a parent container when a new object is created.
marking_points.quote: When a new object is created, is ACL is inherited from that of the enclosing container, e.g. a directory.

marking_points.point: Capabilities are supported by only a small subset of UNIX-like operating systems.
marking_points.quote: Capabilities are supported by only a small subset of UNIX-like operating systems (e.g. Linux with kernel versions above 2.4.19)

marking_points.point: Access control structures must meet requirements such as expressing control policies, verifiability, scalability, and manageability.
marking_points.quote: Requirements for access control structures: an ability to express control policies veriﬁability of correctness. scalability and manageability

questions.question: State six key characteristics of the Bell-La Padula (BLP), Biba, and Chinese Wall security models as described in the formal security model lecture.

marking_points.point: BLP model is described as access control only
marking_points.quote: Bell-La Padula (BLP) model: access control only

marking_points.point: Biba model adds integrity verification
marking_points.quote: Biba model: additional integrity verification

marking_points.point: Chinese Wall model identifies conflicts of interest
marking_points.quote: Chinese Wall model: identification of conflicts of interest

marking_points.point: Chinese Wall is an access control confidentiality policy, not an integrity policy
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: Chinese Wall policy addresses conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash’s Chinese Wall Policy is designed to address a very specific concern: conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor.

marking_points.point: Chinese Wall accesses are sensitive to the history of past accesses
marking_points.quote: The Chinese Wall is an access control policy in which accesses are sensitive to the history of past accesses.

questions.question: Discuss the security mechanisms provided by Windows for user account and object management, and explain why their complexity can be a security risk.

marking_points.point: Windows provides complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: DACLs enable fine-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconfiguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are processes and threads, and their security credentials are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: Tokens provide a principal/subject mapping and may contain additional security attributes.

marking_points.point: Tokens are inherited (possibly with restrictions) during creation of new processes.
